COMMUNIQUER AVEC WILLIAM SHER 


Supervisory personnel in plants and offices are becoming 
increasingly aware of the need for new skills to cope with rapid 


changes in the tempo and nature of contemporary business. 


Attesting that this awareness matches that of senior management 


is the growth of Industrial Management Clubs in Canada. 


In Montreal alone, some 500 NCOs of industry belong to the 
local chapter. Sponsored by the Montreal YMCA, its slogan is 


"Making Management Meaningful." 


Most Industrial Management Clubs' chapters in Canada are affiliated 


with the Y, drawing on its resources as required. 


Continued 


Purpose of all these clubs is basically the same; to help 
supervisory personnel develop as individuals so they will better 


understand and fulfill their responsibilities. 


Having just completed its spring educational program and elected 
a new slate of officers, the Montreal chapter is planning for the 


upcoming fall-winter season. 


To sharpen the administrative capabilities of the membership, 
the program will include studies of Employee Relations and 
Productivity, Effective Leadership and Supervisory Techniques, 
Public Speaking for Management, the History of Industrial 


Development, and the Constructive Use of Leisure Time. 


Continued 


The discussion of ways to use leisure time constructively will 
be designed primarily to stretch the individual's capacity to 


enjoy more things more fully. 


There will also be once-a-month discussions with leasing 
authorities on a wide range of topics of interest to supervisory 


personnel. 


As in the past few years, all courses will be in both English 
and French.
